elements.label: Figure 5.10
elements.description: Stacked bar chart. Y-axis: 'Number of workers (millions)', 0 to 25 in steps of 5. Bars are split into 'Has contract' (teal) and 'No contract' (orange). Each sector shows bars for 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018 and 2020 (years labelled on the x-axis). Approximate readings (values not printed, so these are estimates): Agriculture and fishing total ~23.2 (2010), ~24.7 (2012), ~24.0 (2014), ~23.7 (2016), ~22.3 (2018), ~16.2 (2020), with contract share only ~0.3 each year. Mining and quarrying totals ~0.2 or less in all years. Manufacturing total ~8.6, ~8.3, ~8.5, ~8.9, ~9.7, ~13.9 with contract ~3.3, ~3.5, ~4.3, ~4.8, ~5.5, ~7.6. Electricity, gas and water is under ~0.5 in all years. Construction total ~3.3 to ~4.6 with contract ~0.4 to ~0.7. Commerce total ~7.9, ~8.1, ~8.7, ~9.2, ~9.9, ~10.8 with contract ~0.9 rising to ~1.8. Education, health and social work total ~1.8 to ~2.9, mostly contract (~1.8 to ~2.4). Transport, storage and social work total ~1.5 to ~2.2, with contract ~0.5 to ~0.9. Financial, insurance and real estate is under ~1 total, with contract ~0.2 to ~0.6. Public admin total ~1.3 to ~2.0, mostly contract (~1.4 to ~1.6). Other total ~1.0 to ~1.4, mostly no contract. Pattern: agriculture has the most workers but almost none with contracts; manufacturing and commerce hold most contract jobs, and contract jobs rise over time in manufacturing and commerce. Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS.

elements.label: Figure 5.11
elements.description:
Two stacked bar charts of number of workers (millions) by sector and skill level of jobs. Legend (2020 panel): High-skilled non-manual (teal), Low-skilled non-manual (orange), Skilled manual (grey), Unskilled manual (yellow). Sectors on x-axis: Agriculture and fishing; Mining and quarrying; Manufacturing; Electricity, gas and water; Construction; Commerce; Transport, storage and communication; Education, health, social work; Financial, Insurance, real estate; Public admin; Other.

Top panel, 'Number of workers by skill level of jobs in 2010' (y-axis 0 to 25). Approximate readings: Agriculture and fishing total ~24, with skilled manual ~7.7 and unskilled manual ~16 on top, high-skilled ~0.2. Mining and quarrying ~0.4. Manufacturing ~7.1 (skilled manual ~5.5, unskilled ~0.6, high-skilled ~0.6). Electricity, gas and water ~0.3. Construction ~3.2 (skilled manual ~2.1, low-skilled ~0.5, unskilled ~0.5). Commerce ~5.8 (mostly low-skilled non-manual ~4.4 and skilled manual ~0.6). Transport, storage and communication ~3.6 (low-skilled ~1.7, skilled ~1.0). Education, health, social work ~2.2 (high-skilled ~2.0). Financial, insurance, real estate ~0.7. Public admin ~1.6 (high-skilled ~1.1). Other ~1.1.

Bottom panel, 'Number of workers by skill level of jobs in 2020' (y-axis 0 to 25). Approximate readings: Agriculture and fishing total ~17.5 (unskilled manual ~13.3, skilled manual ~4.1, high-skilled ~0.2). Mining and quarrying ~0.2. Manufacturing ~11.4 (skilled manual ~8.8, unskilled ~1.0, low-skilled ~0.6, high-skilled ~1.0). Electricity, gas and water ~0.4. Construction ~4.8 (unskilled ~1.5, skilled ~2.9, high-skilled ~0.4). Commerce ~7.4 (low-skilled ~5.2, unskilled ~0.6, skilled ~0.6, high-skilled ~0.8). Transport, storage and communication ~5.0 (skilled ~1.3, low-skilled ~2.6, high-skilled ~0.6, unskilled ~0.5). Education, health, social work ~2.6 (high-skilled ~2.3). Financial, insurance, real estate ~1.3. Public admin ~1.8 (high-skilled ~1.1). Other ~1.7.

Pattern: unskilled manual jobs in agriculture fall sharply from 2010 to 2020, while high-skilled non-manual jobs are concentrated in education, health and social work and public admin. Note: See Table A.5.1.1 for skill categorization. Source: World Bank calculations using LFS 2010 and 2020.
